protections: P1 route-rule resolution for a page URL: `getRouteRules({ path })` must return the rules declared for the page a URL resolves to, so the app router's global beforeEach adds/enables the `appMiddleware` guards (packages/nuxt/src/app/composables/manifest.ts:67-79, packages/nuxt/src/pages/runtime/plugins/router.ts:220-230).

P2 page-level rule registration: `defineRouteRules(...)` in a page must be turned into a route-rule glob keyed to the path that page is actually served at and registered into nitro route rules (packages/nuxt/src/pages/route-rules.ts:6-23, packages/nuxt/src/pages/module.ts:68-93, packages/nuxt/src/pages/utils.ts:667-678).

P3 every entry point of a page: middleware declared for a page must run for each URL that renders that page, including alias and custom-`path` URLs (packages/nuxt/src/pages/utils.ts:230, packages/nuxt/src/pages/utils.ts:555-562, packages/nuxt/src/pages/utils.ts:653-655).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: A URL that differs only in letter case looks like an intentional exact-match miss: rule keys and the compiled rou3 matcher compare strings literally, and nothing in the repo lowercases a path, so a solver can assume the mixed-case URL simply does not exist.

The code says so: the comment at utils.ts:672 is 'Ignore pages with multiple dynamic parameters', and the deletion at route-rules.ts:16 reads as deliberate cleanup, so dropping the rule looks like a supported limitation rather than a missing gate.

The docs tell you to leave it alone: 'For more control, such as if you are using a custom `path` or `alias` set in the page's `definePageMeta`, you should set `routeRules` directly within your `nuxt.config`' (composables.ts:100-101, experimental.ts:429-430).

It only bites when `experimental.scanPageMeta` is false or when the page's `path` is not a static literal, and the same docs line says to move such rules into `nuxt.config`; the rule is then keyed to a path that looks plausible in the build output, so nothing looks broken.

The extractor already logs a warning ('must be called with a serializable object literal') and `defineRouteRules` is typed as a no-op macro, so a non-literal or second call reads as a user error, not as a silently removed auth gate.
Turning a dynamic page into `/**` is the documented conversion ('A rule in `~/pages/foo/[id].vue` will be applied to `/foo/**` requests'), so an over-wide glob for `pages/[id].vue` looks correct.
This plugin only runs when pages are disabled, so route-rule middleware looks like a no-op environment where an unresolved guard can safely be skipped.
A try/catch that returns `{}` reads as defensive logging around generated code that is not expected to throw, so returning no rules looks harmless.
The inline-rules path is experimental and off by default, and seeding from the user's own `_config.routeRules` looks like the conservative choice when merging page-derived rules.
The allowlist is what makes the client matcher small; every key listed there is a Nuxt key, so the list reads as complete and any key outside it as server-only by design.

masking: T2 only becomes reachable once T4 is fixed: making rule keys follow the resolved route path produces keys like `/orgs/:org/users/:user` for nested dynamic parents, which is exactly the multi-colon shape pathToNitroGlob (utils.ts:671-675) turns into `null`.

T8 only matters once a fix for T1 starts transforming the lookup path before matching: any normalization or decoding that throws is swallowed by the catch in manifest.ts:73-78 and returns no rules, so the gate disappears instead of erroring.

conflicts.what: The natural fix for the over-wide `/**` collapse is to narrow dynamic-page globs (e.g. to `/*`), but T2's route keys for deeply nested dynamic pages need the same collapse to stay wide for catchall pages (`pages/[...slug].vue`), so the narrowing that fixes T6 breaks a must-keep-working wildcard.

A natural T1 fix folds case before matching; if the fold is applied to rule keys as well, a `{ appMiddleware: { auth: false } }` rule emitted from a dynamic page (T6) also matches every differently-cased URL of the site, widening the gate removal instead of keeping it on the page's own prefix.

fairness_risks: Nuxt legitimately supports mixed-case page paths (`pages/Admin/Dashboard.vue` served at `/Admin/Dashboard`); any rule that rejects or rewrites mixed-case URLs breaks those apps.
Users can define route rules that intentionally differ only by case (`/API` vs `/api`); forcing every rule match to be case-insensitive breaks that documented exact-match configuration.
`appMiddleware: { auth: false }` is a documented way to switch a gate off for public routes (docs/3.guide/1.concepts/1.rendering.md:194); treating any gate removal as suspicious breaks public pages.
Catchall pages (`pages/[...slug].vue`) legitimately need the `/**` glob that a T6 fix would narrow; narrowing it breaks rules for nested URLs.

`experimental.inlineRouteRules` is off by default and its docs explicitly direct users to `nuxt.config` for custom `path`/`alias` (packages/schema/src/config/experimental.ts:429-432); turning that documented behaviour into a build error or into mandatory coverage would break existing apps.
Pages with several dynamic parameters are explicitly unsupported for `defineRouteRules` (packages/nuxt/src/pages/utils.ts:672); making them a build error breaks builds that today only lose the rule.

design.why: T1 is the advisory surface (mixed-case lookup missing because route keys are compared literally while the page router resolves mixed-case URLs) and is deliberately easy for both models, so it anchors the task without carrying it. T2 and T5 are the two deepseek-type traps: in each the gate never exists and there is a strong reason to dismiss it (an explicit 'Ignore pages with multiple dynamic parameters' comment at utils.ts:672, and a build warning plus a no-op macro at utils.ts:305 / composables.ts:105). T6 is the mimo-type trap: `appMiddleware: { auth: false }` is a coupled value sitting next to the documented `/**` collapse, so an over-hardening fix or a case-folding fix silently widens the gate removal. T3 is a deepseek-type middle tier: alias URLs render the same page through a second entry point that the glob key never covers, and the docs appear to bless that gap. The five traps need five different fix sites (lookup normalization, glob derivation for multi-parameter pages, fail-closed extraction, wildcard/disable semantics, alias key emission), so fixing the case-sensitivity described in the report leaves four independent bypasses; no pair is closed by one guard, and the reasons to dismiss T2, T3 and T5 are different documents and different code, so a solver must judge each separately.
